#3012. Which Long-Term Bond ETF Is the Better Buy: State Street’s SPLB or iShares’ TLT?

One fund lends to companies and pays more. The other lends to the U.S. government and offers more safety. Here is how to choose.

The State Street SPDR Portfolio Long Term Corporate Bond ETF (SPLB +0.29%) offers lower costs and corporate credit exposure, while the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT +0.05%) provides high-liquidity access to long-term government debt.

Both funds target the long end of the maturity spectrum, meaning they are highly sensitive to interest rate movements. However, they differ in credit risk: one relies on the full faith and credit of the U.S. government, while the other holds thousands of corporate obligations.

Beta measures price volatility relative to the S&P 500; beta is calculated from monthly returns over the available fund history (up to five years). The 1-yr return represents total return over the trailing 12 months. Dividend yield is the trailing-12-month distribution yield.

The State Street fund is considerably more affordable with a 0.04% expense ratio. It also offers a higher payout, with a yield gap of 1.07 percentage points over the iShares fund, reflecting the additional risk premium of corporate debt.

State Street SPDR Portfolio Long Term Corporate Bond ETF focuses on U.S. dollar-denominated, investment-grade corporate bonds with maturities of at least 10 years. It is highly diversified with 2,971 holdings; no single position exceeds 0.34% of the portfolio. This fund was launched in 2009. State Street SPDR Portfolio Long Term Corporate Bond ETF has paid $1.31 per share over the trailing 12 months, which on its recent ~$20.9 share price works out to a 6.3% yield.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF holds a much more concentrated portfolio of 49 U.S. Treasury securities with maturities exceeding 20 years. Its largest positions include Treasury Bond 4.63% 05/15/2054 at 4.13%, Treasury Bond 4.75% 05/15/2055 at 4.08%, and Treasury Bond (old) 5.00% 05/15/2056 at 4.06%. This fund was launched in 2002. iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF has paid $4.23 per share over the trailing 12 months, which on its recent ~$81.7 share price works out to a 5.2% yield.

For more guidance on ETF investing, check out the full guide at this link.

Long-term bonds have not been easy to own lately, and neither of these funds has made investors whole over the past five years. Still, SPLB has held up better than iShares' TLT, and that steadier record makes it a strong pick for investors who want bond income for the long haul.

SPLB owns roughly 3,000 corporate bonds, so you get the higher yield of corporate debt without betting on any one company. Companies have to pay more than the government to borrow, which is why SPLB pays more income than TLT. It also costs far less and had a smaller 5-year maximum drawdown. TLT owns only U.S. Treasuries, so default risk is minimal, and its huge size makes it easy to trade. That makes it a common safe haven when stocks get shaky.

Even though SPLB is much smaller, its lower fee and extra income give long-term holders a real edge. If avoiding default risk is your top priority, TLT is the simple choice. For most long-term investors who can handle some corporate credit risk, SPLB looks like the better buy.

Tracking the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick the right dividend stocks, as these experts assign their ratings after an in-depth analysis of a company's financials and ability to pay dividends consistently.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Downstream energy company Phillips 66 (PSX) is this week's first dividend pick. With a quarterly dividend $1.27 per share (annualized dividend of $5.08), PSX offers a yield of 2.25%. In reaction to Q2 results, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reaffirmed a buy rating on Crescent Energy stock with a price target of $18. He noted continued strength in the company's performance, with second-quarter oil production and cash flow surpassing the Street's expectations.

"CRGY's cash flow exceeded expectations by 10%, reinforcing its trajectory of capital efficiency," said Richardson.

The 5-star analyst highlighted that Crescent raised its full-year oil production guidance, citing the effective integration of the Vital Energy acquisition. Additionally, the analyst noted that Crescent's capital spending is and heading toward the lower end of management's prior guidance, indicating disciplined financial controls.

Finally, Viper Energy (VNOM) is effectively controlled by Diamondback Energy. Viper owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests in oil-weighted basins, mainly the Permian in West Texas. Viper recently announced its Q2 2026 results and declared a 32% hike in its base dividend, effective in the third quarter of 2026. "Viper has delivered, and we forecast will continue to deliver, one of the highest production per share growth profiles in our royalty universe" through the end of 2027, said Bilkoski. He believes Viper deserves a premium valuation, given its above-average growth.

Total revenues grew 7.2% year-over-year, supported by a 7.4% increase in mobile services revenue and 2.7% growth in fixed revenues. Profitability climbed at an even faster pace. EBITDA rose 10% with the margin reaching 44.5%, 1.1 percentage points above the previous year.

This performance was also reflected in cash generation. Operating cash flow totaled BRL 12.7 billion in the first 9 months, up 13.5%, while free cash flow amounted to BRL 7.3 billion. Over the same period, net income advanced 23.3% to BRL 5.3 billion. Our robust cash generation and balance sheet give us flexibility to invest in future opportunities while continuing to deliver attractive returns to our shareholders. We have already committed BRL 7.3 billion in shareholder remuneration in 2026 and still have interest on capital and buyback program at our disposal. Moving to Slide 4. The ongoing transformation of our revenue mix remains a key driver of Vivo's consistent top line growth.

Total revenues reached BRL 16 billion in the quarter, increasing 7.2% year-over-year. Mobile service revenues advanced 7.4%, supported by a 9.1% increase in postpaid, while FTTH revenues rose 5.7%. Handsets and electronics also made a strong contribution, up 26.6% compared with last year. During the quarter, we rebalanced Vivo Total revenues, aligning the allocation of mobile and fiber with prices that better reflect the market reality of each product. This does not change the underlying trend with services revenues maintaining a healthy pace, up 6% year-over-year. Beyond the headline growth, the composition of our revenues also continues to evolve favorably.

Recurring revenues now represent 84.9% of service revenues, 1.6 percentage points higher than a year ago, further enhancing the resilience of our revenue base. New businesses continue to gain relevance, accounting for 12.5% of total revenues in the last 12 months. This progression reflects our ability to deepen customer relationships and capture opportunities beyond traditional connectivity. Turning to Slide 5. Our mobile business delivered another quarter of high-quality expansion, combining a growing customer base, higher monetization and disciplined churn. Total mobile accesses reached 106.4 million, up 3.4% year-over-year. Excluding M2M and Dongles, our postpaid base expanded to 53.4 million accesses, supported by over 900,000 net additions in the quarter. Monetization also strengthened.

Mobile ARPU reached a new high of BRL 32.9 with the underlying trend remaining positive even when excluding the previously mentioned impact from the rebalance of Vivo Total revenue. Meanwhile, postpaid churn stood at just 1%, underscoring the loyalty of our customer base. In prepaid, we brought to the market an innovative value proposition that goes beyond connectivity. Our new flagship offer starts at BRL 35 for 30 days and incorporates additional benefits such as discount of up to 60% in drugstores through Vale Saúde Farma as well as Google Cloud storage. 5G is also playing an increasingly important role in our premium positioning.

Our 5G customer base now totals 28.1 million, representing 1/3 of mobile access, excluding machine-to-machine and Dongles. And for the third consecutive year, Opensignal recognized Vivo as the fastest 5G network in the world. Together, these indicators highlight Vivo's unique ability to combine scale, monetization and loyalty, allowing us to create a more compelling customer experience. On Slide 6, our fiber business maintains a healthy trajectory, driven by network expansion, convergence and superior service quality. We ended the quarter with 8.4 million FTTH access, up 10.8% year-over-year. Vivo Total remained the main engine behind this performance, rising 27.8% year-over-year to 4 million access. Notably, growth has also come with excellent customer retention.

Fiber churn declined once again, reaching low levels at just 1.4% despite the continued expansion of our customer base. FTTH ARPU also improved year-over-year when excluding the rebalancing associated with Vivo Total. Network utilization is improving as well. Our footprint now covers 32.4 million homes and take-up rate advanced 1 percentage point to 26%, supported by 213,000 FTTH net additions in the quarter. Quality remains a key differentiator. We were ranked first in 4 broadband Internet performance categories in nPerf's worldwide survey among large countries, reinforcing the strength of the connectivity experience we provide. Moving to Slide 7.

Our B2C ecosystem is enabling us to capture a greater share of our customers' digital lives, combining our superior connectivity with an increasingly broad portfolio of services. On the last 12-month basis, B2C revenues reached BRL 47.5 billion, up 7.6% year-over-year. Connectivity revenues rose 6.4%, while new businesses increased 37.1% to BRL 2.3 billion. These deeper relationships are translating directly into higher monetization. Monthly B2C revenue per RGU climbed to BRL 69.8 from BRL 64.6 a year ago across a base of 56.7 million RGUs. Our new businesses are also scaling rapidly across multiple verticals. Consumer electronics advanced 69.4%, health and wellness rose 46.4%, OTTs increased 30.5% and financial services were up 13.6%.

Together, these activities now account for 3.6% of total revenues. We continue to enrich this ecosystem with offers that extend well beyond traditional telco services. During the quarter, Vivo became the first telecom operator in Latin America to launch AppleCare services. Already more than 15%of iPhone Pro devices sold in Vivo stores include the service, providing an encouraging early indication of customer demand for integrated protection solutions. In addition, we launched new streaming bundles starting at BRL 49.90 where customers can combine up to 6 streaming services for a fixed monthly fee with the convenience of managing their subscriptions and paying for everything through a single bill.

By progressively bringing connectivity, entertainment, financial services, health, AI and consumer technology into the same ecosystem, we are deepening customer relationship, creating new monetization opportunities and ultimately unlocking greater customer lifetime value. Turning to Slide 8. B2B is another key avenue for diversification as we broaden our capabilities to address the technology needs for companies of all sizes. On a last 12-month basis, B2B revenues reached BRL 14.1 billion, up 7.1% year-over-year. Connectivity expanded 4.7%, while digital B2B grew 10.9% and now accounts for 8.9% of Vivo's total revenues. This momentum is broad-based across our digital capabilities. Cybersecurity increased 15.9%. Cloud services advanced 12.4%. Digital solutions were up 12.1% and IoT and messaging progressed 6%.

Our ambition, however, goes beyond selling individual products. We are bringing together connectivity with digital services to offer integrated solutions that address increasing complex enterprise needs. A good example is our partnership with Palo Alto Networks for new Agentic Security Operations Center. The solution incorporates AI agents into threat prevention, detection and response processes alongside 24/7 monitoring, local specialists and Telefónica's global cybersecurity ecosystem. These capabilities strengthen Vivo's positioning as a leading provider of integrated digital solutions and allow us to address a wider share of our enterprise customer technology needs. Next, on Slide 9, we showcase our constant drive to innovate and enhance the quality and reach of our connectivity with the launch of Vivo Satélite.

Through our partnership with Starlink, Vivo became the first mobile operator in Brazil to cover nearly 100% of the country. By complementing our terrestrial network, we have extended our coverage into rural and remote areas without material impact on profitability. At the core of this initiative is direct-to-device technology, enabling smartphones to connect directly to satellites without relying on terrestrial infrastructure. This allows us to expand our geographic footprint well beyond our traditional mobile network that already covers over 98% of the population, but only around 20% of the Brazil's territory.

Currently, more than 50 million eligible Vivo customers are the first in the country to experience this capability, access to messaging, GPS and calls via selected apps available even in the most remote areas of the country. Looking ahead, we have a clear road map that includes the rollout of commercial models across B2B and B2C alongside further improvements in connectivity speeds as the technology evolves. Moving to Slide 10. We are making further progress on our ESG agenda through meaningful engagement and external recognition. On the environmental front, we raised our operational emissions targets for Scopes 1 and 2 from 90% to 95% by 2035, while preserving our net zero commitment by 2035.

We also published our 2026 Climate Action Plan, setting the road map that will guide our transition towards a low-carbon economy. Beyond our own operations, we are actively engaging society in sustainability discussions. Encontro Futuro Vivo 2026 brought together 19 panelists and more than 9 hours of content generating 62 million views. Our efforts are being acknowledged across several dimensions. Vivo placed first among large corporations in the Ethos, Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Assessment ranked in top 10 for the first time ever in the Merco Talent ranking and received the Compliance Program of the Year award for the second consecutive year.

Additionally, we were once again named among Brazil's best companies to work for, recognized as Best IT and Telecom company by Valor Econômico and attained the highest level of governance in FGV's Corporate Governance Maturity Index. Taken together, these achievements demonstrate how climate action, diversity, governance and talent are embedded in our strategy and contribute to sustainable long-term value creation. With that, I will hand it over to Rodrigo, who will take you through our financial performance. Thank you.

Rodrigo Monari: Christian, and good morning, everyone. Turning to Slide 11. Disciplined cost management and operating leverage once again enabled profitability to outpace top line growth, complemented this quarter by gains from migration-related asset sales. Total costs rose 5% year-over-year, below the 7.2% increase in revenues. Cost of operations were broadly stable, while cost of services and goods sold advanced at 15.6%, reflecting the evolution of our business mix. Within this line, the increase in cost of goods sold was consistent with the expansion in consumer electronics revenues and B2B equipment. Cost of services grew moderately 3%, reflecting the evolution of B2B digital services and the continued expansion of B2C offerings. In expenses, we continue to demonstrate solid discipline.

Notably, commercial and infrastructure expenses declined 0.9%, while the provision for bad debt remained at a healthy 1.8% of gross revenue, supported by our robust credit scoring and premium customer base. Other revenues were BRL 365 million in the quarter, including BRL 352 million in gains from copper sales and BRL 14 million from real estate. As a result, EBITDA once again grew at a double-digit rate, reaching BRL 7.1 billion, while the margin expanded by 1.1 percentage points to 44.5%. These results demonstrate our continued ability to combine cost discipline, operating leverage and portfolio transformation to convert top line expansion into stronger profitability.

On Slide 12, we remain focused on the strategic investments that support our future development while progressively reducing the capital intensity of the business. CapEx totaled BRL 7.2 billion in the first 9 months of '26, representing 15.2% of revenues, down from 15.7% in the same period last year, underscoring our continued improvement in capital efficiency. Our investments remain concentrated mainly on our strategic infrastructure, including the continued expansion of 5G and fiber. At the same time, operating performance is translating into strong cash generation. In the first 9 months of the year, operating cash flow before leases reached BRL 12.7 billion, 13.5% higher year-over-year. After leases, the figure stood at BRL 8.4 billion, up 17%.

This improvement is also evident in our cash flow margins. On a last 12-month basis, operating cash flow margins before leases reached 27.2%, while the after-lease margin advanced to 18.1%. These figures highlight the scalability of our model. We continue to invest in network quality and future opportunities while converting an increased share of revenues into cash. Moving to Slide 13. Our solid operating performance is turning into higher net income and robust free cash flow generation. Net income reached BRL 5.3 billion in the first 9 months of the year, increasing 23.3% versus previous year. In the third quarter alone, we recorded BRL 2.5 billion, up 30.1% year-over-year, making for another quarter of strong bottom line growth.

Free cash flow amounted to BRL 7.3 billion in the first 9 months, 6.1% above the same period last year. In the third quarter, it reached BRL 2.4 billion, advancing 37.7% year-over-year. On a last 12 months basis, this represents a free cash flow yield of 10%. Our balance sheet also remains very strong. Excluding leases, we closed September with a net cash position of BRL 2.4 billion. Even considering leases, net debt stood at BRL 13.8 billion, equivalent to only 0.5x EBITDA. The combination of higher earnings, cash generation and low leverage provide us with a significant financial flexibility to invest in future opportunities while continuing to deliver attractive returns.

Finally, on Slide 14, we continue to improve our levels of shareholder remuneration and confirm our guidance for the year. As of today, we already disbursed BRL 7 billion to investors with an additional BRL 325 million interest on capital that will be paid in December this year, totaling over BRL 7.3 billion in remuneration. In addition, BRL 1 billion remains available under our current share buyback program through February 27. Notably, with 2 months remaining in the year, we have already declared 4.5% more interest on capital than the entire year of '25, underscoring how value creation to shareholders remain a main pillar of our strategy.

Our operating performance, growing cash generation and solid financial position give us confidence in meeting our guidance for '26, while maintaining the flexibility to continue investing in business and preserving a sound capital structure. As always, our approach is centered on disciplined capital allocation, investing in Vivo's long-term development while delivering compelling returns to our shareholders. Thank you. We are now ready to take your questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Luis Chagas of XP.

Luis Chagas: Congrats on the results. I have 2 questions here. The first one regards prepaid pricing. You recently raised prepaid prices. So how did you see the reaction from customers and from competitors here? And the second question regards OpEx. We saw that commercial and infra costs fell year-over-year, even with the higher commercial activity. Is the third quarter level a good run rate? Or did the one-offs help this quarter? And how much of the renegotiation and FiBrasil savings is still to come?

Christian Gebara: Luis, thank you for the question. So as I said, we just launched a new offer. We are moving price up in the prepaid. Only to remind you, like quarters ago, we already took off WhatsApp from the offer. And now we are trying to move it above the BRL 30 that is the common offer in the market. So we launched this new one that is BRL 35, 30 days. And apart from the data, it also offers like discount in drug stores, and additionally, we also included a cloud storage, a Google Cloud storage. So we started like a few weeks ago.

Difficult to tell you what's going to be the impact, but we are very confident about the movements that we are making in the mobile segment. I think our results are a reflection of that. We do believe that we need to be changing or moving price up to be able to upsell. So now we have this prepaid offer is BRL 35. We have the control, the hybrid entry point also with increase in front book and in the customer base that we had during the year. And we are also offering like new opportunities to cross-sell digital services to both segments. So that's the movement that we have.

As you saw, our postpaid grew 9.1%, prepaid 2.9% negative, but we could see increase in ARPU and also the frequency of recharge and the amount recharged to our customers in prepaid. It's early to say that is the consequence of the new offer, but we are very positive that we are driving in the right direction. Concerning cost, I think that you see -- I think we presented, I don't know, at [indiscernible], you were asking about the commercial infrastructure. Yes, it was like that. I think the reason here is lower network infrastructure costs.

I think there are some benefits that we are already capturing by the migration, the concession to authorization that with some more quarters, we're going to capture even more. There is a little bit that is from the consolidation of FiBrasil. But more importantly is that we are keeping commercial activity in a very high level. As you could see, our acquisition of customers in both segments, mobile and fiber keep in a very high level. So that's part of the business that we are doing here, try to reduce costs, being more digital and also keeping and capturing savings from the migration from concession to authorization.

Operator: Our next question comes from Gustavo Miele of Goldman Sachs.

Gustavo Miele: I have 2 questions as well. The first one, I think it would be great to hear from you guys quite an update here on the outlook for the competitive environment in the postpaid market. We know that the fourth quarter is usually a bit different from other quarters in terms of competitive landscape because of Black Friday. So if you could comment a bit on how you're seeing the movements from competitors on this specific segment, I think that would be great. This would be the first one. And the second one, more specific to the results. We noted that accounts receivables rose I think it was like BRL 1.1 billion quarter-over-quarter. It was a relevant increase.

So just to understand a bit whether this is maybe one-off? And what would be the effects impacting this specific line of the balance sheet?

Christian Gebara: So Gustavo, thank you for the questions. I'll start to answer and then I may ask Rodrigo to complement. We don't see any change in the fourth quarter performance. Actually, we are very positive about the fourth quarter. We had already in October, Apple launch, the iPhone 18 and also the iPhone Duo that brings people to our stores. So we see the opportunity to sell more. We've been very, very good at selling not only smartphone, but services and convergence. And as I stated, not only insurance, but now AppleCare that we are the first one. So we are driving a flow of customers to our stores. We now started November.

It's always a very busy month digitally, but also physically in our 1,800 stores. So I don't see any movement. Our strategy continue to be the one that I just described before, more specifically in the postpaid that you're asking, we are trying to drive convergence where we have availability of fiber. We grew a lot. The number of convergent customers. Now we reached like in Vivo Total 4 million is our record number. And we still have other convergence to migrate to Vivo Total and other customers that are only fiber that could migrate to also Vivo Total. We are adding more digital service that's also help increase our ARPU.

Apart from the AppleCare that I just described, we are launching a lot of OTTs promotions that put together 3 to 6 streaming OTT, and it drives price from BRL 49.9 per month to up to, I don't know, depending on the ones that you selected. Again, we've been very successful. We are reaching annual revenues of BRL 1 billion in revenues just coming from video and music OTT. So again, playing the game of November and December, optimistic about the flow to stores and online e-commerce and also very confident of our ability to sell more services to those that are coming to our stores to buy either a smartphone or any other electronic device.

Concerning like the receivables, Rodrigo can give you more. Yes, we've been very successful commercially. That has a specific impact in the receivables that we have for this quarter. But it's the region of all this is the success of being able to sell more. And you could see the lines of mobile service, fiber service, but more importantly, also electronics sale. Now we have one record, I think one of the most like the highest -- in volume is the highest, but in growth is one of the highest 26.6% of handset and electronic sales year-over-year when you compare.

So BRL 1.1 billion in a quarter that drove these receivables that we have, but we're going to find ways to mitigate that and to drive it in cash. I don't know if you want to complement anything?

Rodrigo Monari: Gustavo, just to reinforce Christian here is I have no concerns about our account receivables. And I think I always emphasize that cash generation is one of the most important pillar of our strategy. In the last year, free cash flow increased 11.4%. And I'm very confident this year, we can keep the same pace we have seen in the last years.

Operator: The next question comes from Gustavo Farias with UBS.

Gustavo Farias: Congrats on the results. So 2 on my end as well. First one, if you could update us on the capital allocation priorities for 2027 and especially in the light of a consolidating market in fiber and potential M&A activity? And my second question, if you could also comment on any expectations or how you are preparing and any anticipated effects of the tax reform on financials?

Christian Gebara: So Farias, I don't know if I get your first question. So I think the structure of our capital structure, we are always assessing it as I think we described before. We have today a very well adapted to the environment that we live here in Brazil of current high interest rates. So I think that's giving us a lot of benefits. And also, we are being able to remunerate our shareholders using all the mechanisms that we have today available. So again, if we expect taxable base or our earnings before taxes to expand over the coming years, of course, it's also driven by the strong performance that we're having.

Of course, we can access and reassess what is the best capital structure. For the moment, we do believe that we have the right one to face the situation that we have right in Brazil. If we need to do M&A, we have many ways to do that. We are open to M&A. We are accessing targets. We haven't come to any conclusion about anything to be acquired in the near term. But of course, we have conversations that we stated in the market a few weeks ago about preliminary conversations that we are having with one specific ISP.

So again, if it comes to the conclusion that we want to buy someone, we have many ways to find the right mechanism to finance it. Regarding what was the second question? Tax reform. What was can you repeat it, please?

Gustavo Farias: Yes. No, just regarding the tax reform, if you guys have any anticipated expected impacts going forward?

Christian Gebara: I think there is all the challenge of implementing it. So we've been preparing ourselves operationally speaking, to be able to implement the tax reform. Of course, we still don't have all the rules that we need to implement, but whatever is available, it's going to be enough for us to put it in process. We are very confident that in the bottom line, the impact will be neutral for us. We may have some increase in some of the tax depending on what's going to be defined by -- we just have CBS. We don't have the total amount.

And -- but again, we also have the compensation of what we had during our chain that we can compensate some of the tax that we paid during the process. So let's see what's going to be the final number. We're going to be prepared to do it, and we believe that apart from the operational challenge of implementing it, the bottom line impact for Vivo will be neutral.

Operator: The next question comes from Leandro Bastos with Citi.

Leandro Bastos: I have 2 questions also. The first, I wanted to double-click a little on the fiber to mobile reallocation you guys mentioned for Vivo Total. If you can just, I don't know, quantify a little better what was the impact in the quarter and just discuss what has been the rationale for this change? So this would be the first question. And then second, if you could comment a little bit still on mobile. How can we think about the outlook for price ups into next year, especially thinking about postpaid back book given the new context of -- given the new macro backdrop in Brazil, competitive landscape in mobile?

I know there are many moving pieces and maybe a little early to tell. But with the visibility you have today, how can we think about the pricing strategy into next year? So I think those would be my questions.

Christian Gebara: Okay. Thank you. So going to the first one, we had this rebalance of Vivo Total is our convergent offer. The key objective is to better reflect the commercial positioning and the pricing of the bundle. Now of course, there is always the allocation, what is mobile and what is fixed. and we believe that we had to reassess it based on what we see as mobile and fiber service prevailing in the market. We have market price available above the line and below the line. And as a result, we assessed and diagnostic was that we needed to rebalance putting more in mobile plan than in fixed plan.

For us, it's difficult because, of course, we are much more focused on convergent and thinking of the service revenue as we grew 6% or thinking of the total revenue that we grew 7.2%. But if we need to show the 2 revenues separately, we need to assess it based on what the plans that are being marketed both for mobile and for fiber. Having said that, we decided to relocate it with a more close reality of its being practiced in the market for both mobile and fiber based on competition and based in the market dimension. So that's the reason. It doesn't change the service revenue.

It's just more fair in the distribution among the 2 plants if you consider that they could be sold separately. For mobile, we are again, we are -- as I said, we drop up price in prepaid. We are driving up prices based in front book and back book. As you know, we do that normally in April and August. That's what we did in 2026. For instance, 70% of the hybrid was like I'm talking about the back book, had a price increase in April. The rest was in August. The postpaid the same, 78% in April. The rest was in August. Vivo Total, that for us is very important. We had everything 100% of price increase in April.

I don't want to give you in advance what's going to be the right time for this. But okay, if there is inflation, we keep the strategy of moving prices up. And we have like normally twice a year, part in one -- in the first semester, the rest in the second semester. We may keep it or not, but that's what I can share with you. The more important than that is that we are creating new also player are very strong in the prepaid at BRL 35, I think, is an important price point to start with the prepaid. The Lite that is the one based in credit card that there is no credit risk for Vivo.

So we are doing that with annual plans. Also, we raised price. Now the annual plan is starting from BRL 30. Again, its BRL 30, but there is a commitment for 12 months. The postpaid, the family plans, the Vivo Total and again, digital services embedded in all offers to rise ARPU up. So that's the strategy that I can share with you right now.

Operator: The next question comes from Rogério Araújo from Bank of America.

Rogério Araújo: I have just one question on the growth momentum in the mobile market. Vivo has outperformed one of the peers. What do you attribute that better performance from Vivo? And also, do you expect this better relative performance to be sustainable? Everything you could share your thoughts internally would be great.

Christian Gebara: Thank you, Rogério. I believe we proved that it has been sustainable for many quarters. Our growth in postpaid is stable. Our net adds is always in this -- close to this volume of 900,000, 1 million customers. Our churn keeps the same level for many quarters of 1%. And again, we are also proving the market that we can innovate. We innovate with the prepaid offer that I described. We are innovating with digital services. We innovated with the satellite embedded in the offer for me is a key innovation of having Vivo as the only one with full coverage in the whole territory.

As I said before, we cover mobile Internet with 97%, 98% of the country, but our coverage of the territory is closer to 20%. So I think that's, again, a differentiation of having Vivo. And being considered the best 5G in the world is also a proof of our CapEx allocation in improving not only the coverage, but also the capacity and the quality that we provide to our customers. I believe, Rogério, that when you have loyal customers, when the level of satisfaction is very high, when we have the best infrastructure, when we are able to innovate creating new offers, also adding service to them and playing convergent.

I think all the elements are here for us to continue to be leading this market. And that's what we do. And our channel also has been improved online and physical channel, and we've been investing in stores. And I think our strategy to blend products, consumer electronics with services has been very successful and is driving our prices and our revenues. And again, we have our offers. We play above the line, and we use below the line in very specific segments when there is retention in place, we are not aggressive, and that's what is driving also our revenues and the loyalty of our customers with the innovation that we bring to the table.

Rogério Araújo: If I may, a follow-up. Is there a big chunk of that performance related to convergence and the lower churn it brings? Or is like the bulk of that higher performance or not necessarily?

Christian Gebara: In fiber, when -- I have 1.4% of churn -- monthly churn. When is -- that's blended, stand-alone fiber, convergent fiber and Vivo Total fiber. Now we have these 3 type of fiber customers, those that are just stand-alone, those that are converted, but not in Vivo Total and those that are Vivo Total. The Vivo Total compared to the stand-alone, the churn in fiber is 1 percentage point lower, okay? So it has a clear -- and in postpaid, we keep 1% for many quarters. So again, I think both of them are being impacted.

Operator: The next question comes from Daniel Federle from Bradesco BBI.

Daniel Federle: The first one is a follow-up on the pricing strategy. My question, do you believe it will be able to continue increasing back book prices in the same real terms that Vivo has done over the years because we are talking about an inflation going above 5%. Probably the tax reform will require at least like 1, 2 percentage points pass-through to final price and the usual real rate increase is 2%, 3%. So we are talking about more or less like a 10% increase in back book price. Do you feel it's possible given intense competition, weak macro conditions and probably a wide gap to the front book price? So the first question is if it's doable or not?

And the second question regarding the B2B digital services revenue, that seems to be decelerating in the third quarter. So more like additional color if that's a trend or more like a weak quarter and then rebound, so more details.

Christian Gebara: For the question. For the first one, the answer is yes, is what I can share. It's part of our business. So that's what we're going to continue to do. So the answer is yes. And in the B2B digital revenues, what I see here, commercially speaking, is that we're expanding our reach. So I'm increasing the penetration of digital service in my B2B customer base, both in the SMEs, but also in the large corporations. But again, the macroeconomic environment is impacting the affordability of my customers. I'm not losing customers. I'm getting more customers, but maybe some of them are postponing plans that they had before due to macro impact. So again, we continue to expand penetration.

It is around 15%. We want to be much, much larger than that. We want more customers buying from us. We've been able to achieve this, but affordability individually by single customer, specifically in some verticals, in some segments, it's been lower due to macro. Let's see what's going to be the future, but we continue to have the right channel, the right portfolio and the desire to increase even more penetration of digital services in B2B.

Daniel Federle: If I may, just a follow-up on the first one. Do you think it's possible to increase back book prices by 9%, for example, even without an increase in the front book prices. Don't you think...

Christian Gebara: Our strategy is always aligned front with back. But I'm not giving you the number now.

Operator: The next question comes from Victoria Antonello from JPMorgan.

Victoria Alcaria Antonello: I have 2 questions on our side. The first one is regarding profitability. So how should we think about profitability going forward? What are the main drivers that we should see in the next quarters in terms of margins? And the second one is regarding Vivo Satélite. So at the moment, the Vivo Satélite is free for 12 months for consumers, right? And what's the monetization plan after that period of 12 months? And at the beginning, are you seeing any clear usage among the eligible customers you have?

Christian Gebara: So thank you, Victoria. We have like it available for 50 million customers, particularly in B2C. So 50 million customers can use today, what we saw is 10 million already used it. So 10 million out of the 50 million already used it. So it's a very important adoption considering that we launched it a few weeks ago. Monetization is not just in 1 year before that in B2B, 3 months, we have filed B2B. We are not sharing what's going to be the commercial plans because we haven't officially communicated. But of course, we will be able to monetize both in B2B after 3 months and also in B2C after 12 months, as you correctly stated.

EBITDA, we are very confident about the evolution of -- I don't know if you talk about profitability of net income of EBITDA. EBITDA, represented a 10% increase, I think, for us is one of the highest number that we presented in the last years. The margin is also 1.1 percentage point. I think here, there is a combination of many things. I described it before, our efficiency driven by the migration from concession to authorization. We are also doing a lot of digitalization in customer care and back-office tasks. Now AI is bringing us already results, and we'll be able to announce more in the coming quarters, but we are scaling AI-driven solutions across the operation.

And again, we are growing in revenues. We are growing in services, talking about going just after the EBITDA. We're also growing a lot our services, as I stated, 12.5% already coming from digital service, where there is no consumption of CapEx. And the profitability is the final one then net income, many other things coming along. As also we described, we -- I think in the last quarter, we talked about the end of the acceleration of depreciation driven by the legacy technologies. So you could see now the number already there because depreciation is lower because we already depreciated everything that we had in legacy technology.

So I think our results, they come in this direction for many quarters. So revenue, 7.2%, EBITDA at 10%. If you take from EBITDA, the CapEx, we are talking about 13.5%. If you take leases, 17%. And then if you go to the free cash flow this quarter was 37.7%. But as Rodrigo said before, our CAGR in the last year has been over 7% and net income, again, 23.3% in the 9 months that we have right up to now, specifically in the quarter, 30%. So I think it's a lot of things going -- coming together that is, again, reflecting the strategy that we've been defending for many years that is bringing results.

So that's the answer, and that's what we expect to continue in the next quarter.

Operator: The next question comes from Phani Kanumuri from HSBC.

Phani Kumar Kanumuri: The first one is on your depreciation. It seems like it is down almost BRL 400 million quarter-on-quarter. Is this all related to the migration? Or is there some other impact coming here? The second one is regarding the leases. The leases have been up around 7.7% on the principal part. How do you expect this to trend going forward?

Christian Gebara: Phani, so as I -- thank you for the question. As I said in the previous answer to Victoria, we anticipated in the last quarter that D&A expenses were already expected to decline because supported by the commissioning of legacy technology. So the copper-related assets became fully depreciated this quarter. So the depreciation expenses reduced by BRL 282 million, okay? So that's the explanation about the evolution of depreciation. In leases, Rodrigo can complement.

Rodrigo Monari: Phani, regarding leases, if you consider the payment of interest, too, with principal payments, you have a 5.7% increase in this quarter. But if you look at the last 12 months basis, the increase is only 3.6%. So we are under -- below the mobile revenues increase in the last few years. So we are confident we can keep this pace in the future.

Christian Gebara: So as we stated before, our year-over-year -- last 12 months evolution of leases should be below the evolution of the mobile service revenue. So if you take third quarter, last 12 months, year-over-year evolution, our leases increased in 3.6%, well below the evolution of our mobile service revenues.

Phani Kumar Kanumuri: Yes. Maybe a quick follow-up there. So have you been able to renegotiate with the tower companies on the pricing or...

Christian Gebara: But that's part of the strategy here. We're negotiating prices. We increased co-location. As we stated before, the number of tenants per site in Brazil is very low when I compare to Europe, for instance, we have 1.4. So we're trying to have more co-location. There are many new vendors also providing new tower companies. So we also have the opportunity also to swap. So it's a combination of the 3. So we've been successful, and we need to expand coverage, but we need to keep the leases under the terms that I described before.

Operator: The question-and-answer section is over. We would like to hand the floor back to Mr. Christian Gebara for the company's final remarks.

Christian Gebara: So thank you, everyone, to participate in our call. Again, this call and these results reconfirm the strategy that we've been following here in the company to grow revenues in a combination of mobile, fiber, convergence, digital services, B2C, B2B in a footprint that's unique for Vivo, being very disciplined in the cost management and also in the CapEx allocation. We didn't talk about that, but CapEx over revenues is also in a positive trend. And that in the end is giving us the return in operating cash flow, free cash flow and also net income that is being part of the remuneration that we have for our shareholders. We are open for other opportunities in M&A.

So that's why we're generating cash. Also, we envision that we could be participating in some of this. And any other questions or remarks that you may have, please reach out to our team here. And this week, we are going to also be talking to some of you in the market. So thank you again for participating, and hope to talk to you soon. Thank you.

Operator: Vivo's conference is now closed. We thank you for your participation and wish you a nice day.

#3003. Airbnb vs. MercadoLibre: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Airbnb's lean marketplace model and MercadoLibre's sprawling Latin American ecosystem pull in very different directions, and the margin gap between them tells a story worth weighing.

Choosing between a global travel leader and a Latin American commerce giant requires balancing high growth against established profitability. Which path is right for your portfolio between Airbnb Inc. (ABNB -3.09%) and MercadoLibre Inc. (MELI +1.46%)?

Airbnb provides a unique global platform for alternative accommodations, while MercadoLibre operates an expansive ecosystem of e-commerce, fintech, and logistics services across Latin America. Both companies benefit from the digital shift in consumer spending, but they navigate very different competitive landscapes and regional economic conditions as they head toward 2027.

Airbnb connects over 5 million hosts with guests seeking unique stays and experiences in over 220 countries, as detailed in its latest annual report for FY 2025. Its two-sided platform offers hosts tools like integrated payments and protection through AirCover, while providing guests with AI-powered search and personalization features. By maintaining a marketplace rather than owning properties, the company stays lean while expanding its presence among travel and tourism stocks.

In FY 2025, revenue reached about $12.3 billion, representing growth of approximately 10.8% compared to the previous year. The company reported net income of about $2.5 billion for the period. While revenue continued to climb, the net margin of roughly 20.4% was lower than in previous years as the company invested in platform updates and marketing.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, indicating a conservative amount of total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio, measuring the ability to cover short-term liabilities, is roughly 1.4x. In FY 2025, free cash flow reached around $4.6 billion, though stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 34.3% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation.

MercadoLibre operates a massive ecosystem in Latin America, which the company detailed in its latest annual report for FY 2025. It integrates a marketplace for buyers and sellers with its Mercado Pago fintech solution and a proprietary logistics network, Mercado Envios, to ensure fast delivery. This integrated approach creates a powerful flywheel where commerce, payments, and logistics reinforce one another for its 136 million unique buyers.

In FY 2025, revenue reached around $28.9 billion, a significant increase of approximately 39.1% compared to the prior year. The company reported net income of roughly $2.0 billion for the same period. While the top line grew rapidly, the net margin was approximately 6.9% as the company focused on market share expansion and its credit business.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.7x, showing how the company uses debt to fund its extensive logistics and credit operations. The current ratio is approximately 1.2x, suggesting a healthy level of liquidity for its day-to-day business. In FY 2025, MercadoLibre generated free cash flow of about $10.8 billion, which is the cash remaining after covering operating costs and capital investments.

Airbnb faces stiff competition from established online travel agencies such as Booking Holdings (BKNG +0.60%) and Expedia Group (EXPE +2.37%), as well as search engines like Alphabet Inc. (GOOG +2.00%). Regulatory challenges pose a major threat, as cities like New York and Barcelona implement strict short-term rental bans that could limit listing growth. Additionally, the company relies heavily on third-party infrastructure from Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN -1.74%) for its cloud services and faces potential reputational risks from third-party misconduct.

MercadoLibre must navigate intense competition from both local players and global rivals like Amazon across its diverse markets. The company is particularly exposed to macroeconomic instability and currency volatility in countries like Argentina and Brazil, which can impact its reported financial results. Furthermore, its expanding credit business introduces significant credit risk, while reliance on Apple Inc. (AAPL +2.04%) for app distribution adds a layer of platform dependency.

Airbnb carries a lower Forward P/E but a much higher P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

MercadoLibre evolved from the 'eBay of Latin America' to something more akin to a combination of Amazon and PayPal Holdings Inc. (PYPL +1.19%). In 2025, the company made large investments in its Brazilian logistics network, cut down the free-shipping threshold in Brazil in June, and nearly doubled its consumer loan book. This drove impressive growth for the company and investors, with an increasing focus on financial services over delivering goods.

Yet the immediate concern with left-of-center Luis Lula winning the Brazilian presidential election last month is that the new administration will start addressing Brazil's high government and consumer debt levels, which will keep interest rates there around their current very high levels. That's bad for a consumer-loan-focused business like MercadoLibre, and shares have been hammered this week as a result.

Long-term, however, such fears are probably overblown. In fact, in the current fiscal year, revenue is expected to jump 45% to $41.9 billion, with slightly higher free cash flow and slightly lower net income. Overall, it's a good picture for MercadoLibre.

Airbnb reported an excellent third quarter of fiscal 2026. The business beat consensus revenue estimates by more than $100 million, reporting $4.87 billion in sales, up nearly 19% from the same period in 2025, driven by a strong increase in booked nights. Foreign markets like India and Latin America, two markets in which Airbnb is seeking growth, have been strong this year. The seasonally weaker fourth quarter should see sales close to $3.3 billion and net income around $488 million.

The business is finding ways to expand its popular travel business, embracing features like buy now, pay later (BNPL) on reservations, a form of short-term lending. The network advantage of Airbnb's history, over 2 billion guest arrivals since 2008, and the lack of host presence on AI (meaning a competitor using AI has little data to scrape to form a competing product) give it a competitive moat.

For the full year, management expects sales of $14.1 billion with net income of $3.2 billion.

MercadoLibre comes at a premium, a level we feel is overextended for a Latin America-dependent stock. Airbnb also isn't cheap, but its North America-based travel customer has historically proven to be the more resilient spender, making that P/E ratio more palatable.

#3002. Ray Dalio says Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

The Bridgewater Associates founder said Bessent's plan to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

"I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma."

Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

The U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio said. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

Bessent said in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

After years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

To solve this, Dalio said the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

First, Dalio said the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the New York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

"All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio said. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic."

Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he said.

Dalio said it's important to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

Dalio said the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed."

To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder said.

Dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

Financial Stability Coordination & Actions

Financial Market Utilities & Infrastructures

For release at 2:30 p.m. EDT Share

The Federal Reserve Board on Thursday requested public comment on two proposals related to establishing a regulatory framework for Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act.

The first proposal would require that Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers fully back their stablecoins with certain permissible reserve assets, such as short-term Treasury bills and certain other high-quality, liquid assets. The proposal would also establish standardized capital requirements to address certain credit and operational risks of payment stablecoin activities, as well as risk management standards, in accordance with the law. Separately, the proposal would introduce rules for Board-supervised firms that safekeep the assets backing payment stablecoins. It would also clarify the permissibility of stablecoin and related activities for Board-supervised banks.

The second proposal would establish a tailored application process for Board-supervised banks applying to issue payment stablecoins. These applicants would be required to submit a business plan and financial information, among other documents. The proposal would also create a process governing appeals, hearings, and final determinations for applications.

The comment period will close 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

#3000. Nasdaq Sell-Off: 2 Stocks to Buy on the Dip and Hold for 5 Years

On Thursday, Nov. 5, two days after the U.S. midterm elections, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped by more than 5%, its worst single-day dip in over a year. The reason behind the sharp sell-off is no secret. Democrats emerged as the winners of the midterm elections, and now that they control both chambers of the U.S. Congress, investors are worried about what that means for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. That's a reasonable worry, but even in this environment, there are attractive stocks worth buying and holding onto at least for the next five years. Here are two great examples to consider: Shopify (SHOP +1.81%) and Axsome Therapeutics (AXSM +5.87%).

Shopify is proving its resilience. Despite a challenging macroeconomic landscape and the threat AI poses to its business, the company's financial results have been pretty strong. In the third quarter, Shopify's revenue increased by 32% year over year to $3.7 billion, driven by a 29.5% increase in gross merchandise volume (GMV) to $119.1 billion.

The company's gross profit jumped 28% year over year to $1.8 billion, while its net income, excluding the impact of equity investments, was $584 million, up 59% compared to the year-ago period. Shopify also posted free cash flow of $816 million at a 22% margin, versus $507 million in the third quarter of 2025 at an 18% margin. Management noted that AI-powered searches are helping boost the company's GMV and revenue.

Shopify has built AI tools to help users find what they want more easily and to help merchants automate tasks and better reach customers. The results are showing up in the company's numbers. But we may still be in the early innings of this tailwind. AI has only just begun to change how people shop -- with agents aiding search and purchases -- and Shopify is positioning itself to capitalize on this as it becomes more common.

Meanwhile, there remains a massive white space in the e-commerce industry. E-commerce transactions still account for fewer than one in five retail transactions in the U.S. Besides doubling down on AI tools, Shopify boasts a deep ecosystem of merchants whose feedback helps it improve its product offering.

This grants the company a competitive edge through network effects. The stock is down 6% this year, but it has performed well since mid-May, and could beat the market over the next five years.

Axsome Therapeutics is a biotech company focused on central nervous system diseases. The drugmaker has outperformed the broader market over the past five years and is well positioned to do so again. Axsome Therapeutics' portfolio of drugs includes Auvelity, currently its biggest growth driver, Sunosi, and Symbravo. Auvelity is approved for depression as well as agitation associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD).

It helped drive strong results during the third quarter. Axsome Therapeutics' revenue increased 52% year over year to $259.7 million. Auvelity's sales jumped 53% year over year to $207.6 million. The medicine is inching closer to a $1 billion annual revenue run rate. It received the label expansion in AD agitation earlier this year, and this new indication already seems to be having an impact.

Axsome Therapeutics noted that, during the third quarter, Auvelity's new-to-brand prescriptions jumped 44% year over year and 21% quarter over quarter, but the same metric among patients 65 and older soared 211% year over year and 99% quarter over quarter.

Management pointed out that "Sequential increases over the past 2 quarters more than doubled the average quarterly increase prior to label expansion in Alzheimer's disease agitation." This is a great sign for the company, especially given the large, unmet opportunity in the AD market.

Axsome Therapeutics could help fill this need, and the company should launch at least a couple of new products, including AXS-12, a medicine for cataplexy in patients with narcolepsy that could earn approval next year.

Axsome Therapeutics boasts several other products in Phase 2 or Phase 3 studies that could support additional approvals or label expansions. Clinical and regulatory milestones, along with strong revenue growth, could jolt the stock and enable Axsome Therapeutics to outperform the market through 2031.
